rationale: I anchored the near-term small-threshold forecasts on observed cyber base rates: ransomware and breach volumes remain high, reports attribute a growing minority of malicious incidents to AI assistance, and $1B economic-loss events are already plausible in cyber even without direct fatalities. Misalignment is assigned low near-term probability for very large harm because current autonomous systems still have limited real-world authority, but rising long-run probability due to increasingly capable agents embedded in infrastructure, finance, military, and R&D; the broad AI category is treated as the approximate union of cyber, bio, misalignment, and other pathways. For global 10%-mortality catastrophes I used XPT/FRI-style superforecaster-versus-expert ranges as an outside view and chose intermediate but relatively conservative values, with AI making up a growing share of long-run catastrophic risk; disempowerment is higher than AI mass-death because it can occur through dependency or control without immediate large mortality.

Top tiers (100M-1B deaths) and the cross-cutting 10%-mortality questions are calibrated against expert/community estimates (Metaculus Ragnarök series ~1-3% for a 10% population fall by 2100; Ord-style x-risk estimates), yielding ~11% for any 10%-mortality catastrophe by 2100, ~6% for an AI-proximate one, and ~17% for AI disempowerment by 2100, with much smaller values by 2030 given deployment and capability lags. results.content: When Anthropic released Claude Opus 4, we activated AI Safety Level 3 (ASL-3) protections, which included deployment measures narrowly focused on preventing the model from assisting with certain tasks related to chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) weapons development. As we noted at the time, this was a precautionary decision—improving model performance on our evaluations meant we could no longer confidently rule out the ability of our most advanced model to uplift people [...] to uplift people with basic STEM backgrounds if they were to try to develop such weapons. Because of our assessment of the potential consequences, a major initial focus of our evaluations and the corresponding safety measures was on biological weapons. In this post, we want to expand on our perspective on AI and biological risk (biorisk). results.content: Uplift studies are well-suited to showing whether an AI system is able to assist non-experts in troubleshooting protocols related to the production of bioweapons. They may also provide insight into whether an AI system can help with the acquisition of materials and equipment required for the creation of a biological threat, support the release or deployment of biological weapons, or facilitate operational execution of the attack and avoid law enforcement detection. [...] | Anthropic | CBRN-3: The ability to significantly assist individuals or groups with basic STEM backgrounds in obtaining, producing, or deploying CBRN weapons. Assessed by comparing what potential attackers could achieve with full model access versus 2023-level online resources, assuming they have funding and up to one year of time to invest, but no initial specialized expertise.  CBRN-4: The ability to substantially uplift CBRN development capabilities of moderately resourced state programs [...] Critical: The model provides a meaningful uplift to an expert’s ability to develop a highly dangerous novel threat or significantly lowers the barriers to a low-skilled actor developing and delivering a known CBRN threat. |

Top tiers (100M-1B deaths) and the cross-cutting 10%-mortality questions are calibrated against expert/community estimates (Metaculus Ragnarök series ~1-3% for a 10% population fall by 2100; Ord-style x-risk estimates), yielding ~11% for any 10%-mortality catastrophe by 2100, ~6% for an AI-proximate one, and ~17% for AI disempowerment by 2100, with much smaller values by 2030 given deployment and capability lags. Internal coherence was enforced: probabilities decrease monotonically with severity, increase with horizon, and the AI-general ladder approximately equals the union of its subcategories plus other AI pathways (e.g., AI-triggered nuclear use).
